assessment.reason: Projected strikeouts sit about three-quarters of a K above 3.5. At +110 the model clears break-even, while paired books sit near it. No material blocker is sourced, but the starter is not confirmed in the excerpts.
assessment.model_case: Gasser has averaged 16 outs over his last five starts at a 0.212 K/BF rate against a 0.207 opponent K rate. That yields about 4.2 projected Ks (median 4). The case rests on normal length; a short postseason hook trims batters faced and erodes the cushion.
assessment.price_case: Main line 3.5 at +110 needs roughly 47.6 percent; four other books imply about the same. The model sits well above that. The 0.25-weight blend is much closer, so the edge depends on trusting the rolling model over the market.
assessment.context_case: The injury snapshot lists Rays absences, including Lux with an uncertain return date, but publication timing is unknown. Articles do not name starters or describe Gasser's leash. Context is unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: World Series managers can pull starters after two trips through the order. If Gasser faces about 17 batters, the expected Ks fall near the line. The market's near-even pricing may already reflect a shorter leash. This bet is correlated with the outs over and shares the same workload risk.

assessment.reason: The projection of about 13 outs barely clears 12.5, so a single early hook flips the result. The market disagrees, and postseason leash risk is not evidently modeled.
assessment.model_case: The last-five average of 16 outs supports length, but the projection is only about 13.05 (median 13), half an out over the line. The model probability depends on a thin margin that a quick postseason trigger can erase.
assessment.price_case: At +120 the line needs roughly 45.5 percent; three other books imply slightly below that. The 0.25-weight blend sits only modestly above break-even. That margin is too fragile given the workload uncertainty.
assessment.context_case: No sourced reporting addresses Gasser's expected pitch count or bullpen plans. The injury snapshot is not relevant to his workload. Context is unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: If Gasser is truly stretched out and pitching well, 16-out outings would clear easily. The market's skepticism could be overstated for a starter recently going deep.

findings.note: ESPN's game page confirms Gasser starts against Freddy Peralta. It lists his postseason line as 9.0 IP with only 6 strikeouts, which works out to about 3 Ks per start in two short outings, under the 3.5 line.

ESPN's World Series preview calls Milwaukee's starters after Misiorowski and Henderson, Gasser included, 'relatively uninspiring.' It says Pat Murphy will lean more on his bullpen in Games 3 and 4, which points to a short leash and fewer batters faced.

MLB.com's Game 3 preview confirms Gasser starts Monday 8 ET at Tropicana Field with a 1.51 ERA in eight appearances since Aug. 26. He has started clinching or pivotal games in the NLDS and NLCS, so the team trusts him. His regular season was 103 K in 109.1 IP, per Savant.

ESPN's World Series preview calls Gasser one of Milwaukee's 'relatively uninspiring' options after Misiorowski and Henderson, and expects Pat Murphy to lean more heavily on his bullpen in Games 3 and 4, which points to a short leash for Gasser.

Gasser's 2026 regular-season splits show 109.1 IP over 20 starts. He pitched in the 5th inning in 18 of 21 games but only 10 times in the 6th, and right-handers hit him much harder (.765 OPS) than left-handers (.552), so the Rays could stack righties. His September was strong: 1.67 ERA.

MLB.com confirms Gasser starts World Series Game 3 at Tropicana Field against Freddy Peralta. It notes he is 2-0 with a 1.51 ERA in eight appearances since Aug. 26, including postseason starts in NLDS Game 4 and NLCS Game 3.
